title: Robust quantum key distribution with imperfections in state preparation and characterization
authors: Yi-Fei Lu, Yan-Yang Zhou, Yang Wang, Xin-Hang Li, Yu Zhou, Xiao-Lei Jiang, Jia-Ji Li, Chun Zhou, Hong-Wei Li, Yu-Yao Guo, Lin-Jie Zhou, Wan-Su Bao
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers an approach for secure communication over quantum channels, based on the principles of quantum mechanics. However, the inevitable imperfections in QKD systems can introduce critical vulnerabilities, posing significant challenges to the deployment of QKD in terms of both practical security and performance. In this work, we present a comprehensive security analysis of QKD in the practical scenarios involving imperfections in modulation spaces. Specifically, our analysis focuses on the imperfections related to encoding, intensity modulation, and their characterization. We provide a unified framework based on the operator dominance method to overcome these issues and achieve a tight estimation of the secret key rate (SKR). The simulation results show that the SKR in practical scenarios, with parameters characterized from commercial QKD systems, closely matches the SKR under ideal conditions. In the finite case, the maximum transmission distance can reach up to 250 km with total pulse number $N=10^{12}$ and the SKR closely approaches the asymptotic limit up to 250 km with $N=10^{14}$. This validates the robustness of our method against imperfections in state preparation and characterization. Furthermore, the feasibility and robustness of method in measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD have also been demonstrated. Our analysis not only promotes advancements in enhancing practical security and performance but also highlights the feasibility of deploying QKD for actual applications.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive security analysis for Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) that accounts for real-world imperfections in state preparation and characterization. By introducing a unified framework based on the operator dominance method, the authors demonstrate that the achievable secret key rate remains robust and close to the ideal limit. This validates the practical deployment potential of QKD systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses critical vulnerabilities in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) caused by inevitable imperfections in state preparation and state characterization in practical systems.
main_result: The proposed method validates QKD's robustness, showing that the Secret Key Rate (SKR) under practical imperfections closely matches the ideal theoretical limit, even up to 250 km.
method: A unified framework based on the operator dominance method is employed to provide a tight security analysis for QKD, accounting for encoding, intensity, and characterization flaws simultaneously.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), covering single-photon and decoy-state protocols, including Measurement-Device-Independent (MDI) QKD, utilizing weak coherent sources.
key_observables: Secret Key Rate (SKR), Fidelity, Phase Error Rate ($e_x$), and joint measurement probabilities $Y(z)_{i,j}$.
important_parameters: Transmission distance (up to 250 km), total pulse number ($N=10^{12}$ or $N=10^{14}$), and parameters characterizing encoding/intensity imperfections.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the qubit model and uses the operator dominance condition to derive bounds, though it notes limitations regarding side-channel effects and sequential state corrections.
paper_structure: The paper develops the security analysis by first establishing bounds for encoding imperfections (single-photon QKD), then extending to intensity imperfections (decoy-state QKD), and finally applying the framework to MDI-QKD, all while using the operator dominance method.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides rigorous, practical security bounds for quantum communication protocols, directly impacting the engineering feasibility of quantum networks.
